title: Outro: True Love Waits
statementMd:
People often harbor various interpretations of life. Some navigate it smoothly, discovering its meaning at the loftiest peaks, while some encounter misfortune time and time again, lamenting the fleeting nature of life akin to the falling of snow, yet burning it to fight for better situations.

Regardless, life is intricate and filled with worthwhile things to explore. For programmers like you, it is reasonable to conceptualize life as touring an infinite graph — a graph consisting of an infinite number of vertices and edges, to be precise. Its vertices, indicating all possibilities of life, are numbered starting from 00, and for every unordered pair of vertex 𝑢u and vertex 𝑣v, if the binary representations of 𝑢,𝑣u,v differ by exactly one bit which is the 𝑤w-th bit from low to high, then there exists an undirected edge between them with weight 𝑤w. For example, the undirected edge (2,6)(2,6) with weight 33 exists in the graph because 2=(10)22=(10)2, 6=(110)26=(110)2, where the third bit is the only bit different, but the edge (5,6)(5,6) does not exist because 5=(101)25=(101)2, 6=(110)26=(110)2, where there are two bits different between the binary representations.

Initially, you stand on vertex 𝑠s, and you believe that true love, not necessarily being a certain person, should inhabit on vertex 𝑡t. Then you begin the tour to seek true love in life from dawn to dusk. Every moment, you feel unsatisfied with the vertex you are currently on and decide to let go of it. Therefore, among all the edges connecting to this vertex, you choose the one with minimum weight, move through it to the other vertex, and permanently cut this edge from the graph (Uh, it seems like swearing never to come back). Since the tour is endless and the faith in true love is boundless, you become interested in when you will reach vertex 𝑡t for the 𝑘k-th time (Particularly, the initial state is regarded as the first time you reach vertex 𝑠s). Find out the number of edges you will cut along the tour, modulo 109+7109+7, or report it's impossible to reach vertex 𝑡t for the 𝑘k-th time.

## Input

The input contains several test cases, and the first line contains a single integer 𝑇T (1≤𝑇≤1051≤T≤105), denoting the number of test cases.

For each test case, the only line contains three integers 𝑠,𝑡,𝑘s,t,k (0≤𝑠,𝑡<2106,1≤𝑘≤1090≤s,t<2106,1≤k≤109), where 𝑠,𝑡s,t are given in binary representation without any extra leading zeros, and 𝑘k is given in decimal representation.

It is guaranteed that the sum of the lengths of binary representations over all test cases does not exceed 107107.

## Output

For each test case, if it's impossible to reach vertex 𝑡t for the 𝑘k-th time, output −1−1 in one line. Otherwise, output the number of edges you will cut in one line, modulo 109+7109+7.

## Note

In the first test case, you will reach vertex 22 for the first time by trail 1−→−−𝑤=10−→−−𝑤=221→w=10→w=22, so there will be 22 edges cut. Also starting from vertex 11, it can be proved that once you let go of vertex 22 when you reach it for the first time, you will really never come back forever. Thus, the answer for the second test case is −1−1.
statementZhMd:
人们常常对人生抱有不同的理解。有些人一路顺遂，在最高的山巅寻得人生的意义；有些人则一次又一次遭遇不幸，感叹人生如落雪般转瞬即逝，却仍燃烧生命，为更好的境遇而奋斗。

无论如何，人生纷繁复杂，充满值得探索的事物。对于像你这样的程序员来说，将人生看作在一张无限图上的旅行也很合理——准确地说，这是一张包含无穷多个顶点和边的图。图中的顶点代表人生的所有可能，从 $0$ 开始编号。对于每一对无序顶点 $u$ 和 $v$，如果 $u,v$ 的二进制表示恰好只有一位不同，且这一位是从低到高的第 $w$ 位，那么它们之间就有一条权值为 $w$ 的无向边。例如，图中存在权值为 $3$ 的无向边 $(2,6)$，因为 $2=(10)_2$、$6=(110)_2$，只有第三位不同；但图中不存在边 $(5,6)$，因为 $5=(101)_2$、$6=(110)_2$，它们的二进制表示有两位不同。

最初，你站在顶点 $s$ 上，并相信真爱应当栖居于顶点 $t$，尽管真爱未必是某个具体的人。于是，你开始了这场从清晨到黄昏、在人生中寻找真爱的旅行。每一刻，你都会对当前所在的顶点感到不满，并决定放下它。因此，你会在与当前顶点相连的所有边中，选择权值最小的一条，沿着它走到另一个顶点，然后将这条边从图中永久删除（呃，这似乎就像发誓永不回头）。由于旅途没有尽头，而你对真爱的信念也没有边界，你开始好奇自己何时会第 $k$ 次到达顶点 $t$（特别地，初始状态视为你第一次到达顶点 $s$）。请求出截至此时你在旅途中删除的边数，对 $10^9+7$ 取模；或者报告不可能第 $k$ 次到达顶点 $t$。

## 输入格式

输入包含多组测试数据，第一行包含一个整数 $T$（$1\le T\le 10^5$），表示测试数据的组数。

对于每组测试数据，唯一一行包含三个整数 $s,t,k$（$0\le s,t<2^{10^6},1\le k\le 10^9$），其中 $s,t$ 以不含多余前导零的二进制表示给出，$k$ 以十进制表示给出。

保证所有测试数据中二进制表示的长度之和不超过 $10^7$。

## 输出格式

对于每组测试数据，如果不可能第 $k$ 次到达顶点 $t$，则在一行中输出 $-1$。否则，在一行中输出截至此时删除的边数，对 $10^9+7$ 取模。

## 说明

在第一组测试数据中，你会沿着路径 $1\xrightarrow{w=1}0\xrightarrow{w=2}2$ 第一次到达顶点 $2$，因此会删除 $2$ 条边。同样从顶点 $1$ 出发，可以证明，当你第一次到达顶点 $2$ 并离开它后，就真的永远不会再回来了。因此，第二组测试数据的答案为 $-1$。
